true_answer: Without intercalation to add days or months to some years, seasons quickly dri in a calendar based solely on twelve lunar months. Lunisolar calendars have a thirteenth month added to some years to make up for the diﬀerence between a full year (now known to be about 365.24 days) and a year of just twelve lunar months. e numbers twelve and thirteen came to feature prominently in many cultures, at least partly due to this relationship of months to years.
